video.title: 9 High-Ticket Services Nobody Is Offering (In Your Town)

summary: Tim Richard lists nine high-ticket local services he says few businesses target, using Ahrefs search volume, keyword difficulty and weak Google map packs as evidence: Venetian plaster, generator installation, accessible bathroom remodels, riding lawn mower repair, luxury restroom trailer rentals, attic fans, stucco repair, EPDM/TPO flat roofing and crawl space encapsulation. He gives job prices (e.g. 3,000-6,000 USD accent walls, 13,000 USD accessible bathrooms, 5,500 USD crawl spaces) and a few second-hand operator results (an Ohio mower repairer profiting 200,000 USD/yr; a restroom trailer operator netting ~60,000 USD in year one). He also pitches a hub model: rank nationally and route jobs to subcontractors. Takeaway: SEO gaps exist in specialist trades, but most require skilled physical work and US-specific demand.

ideas.name: Generator installation marketing hub

ideas.business_model: Lead/job brokerage: take jobs and pay subcontractors (margin not stated)
ideas.customer: Homeowners and businesses wanting standby generators
ideas.problem: Weather outages have roughly doubled; demand exceeds installers

acquisition_channels.details: 'Home generator installation near me' 8,600 searches/month, KD 2, rising trend
Recruit electrical subcontractors nationwide, as he does for junk removal

ideas.delivery: Speaker's model: nationwide website gets jobs, sends them to subcontractors who do the work ('Uber-style').

acquisition.how: SEO/content and paid search can be agent-run; inbound only.

delivery.how: Subcontractors do the physical work; vetting and quality control need humans.

tactics.name: Find low-competition high-ticket trades with keyword data
steps: Look up service keywords in Ahrefs for monthly volume and keyword difficulty (look for KD 0-10)
Check the search trend for rising demand
Search the service + a big city and inspect the map pack: few listings and <30 reviews mean an opening
Build a site with pages dedicated to the exact service term

quote.text: If we look at the Google business listing showing up
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

tactics.name: Be the marketing hub, subcontract the work
steps: Build one national brand website targeting a service in many areas
Send each job to a subcontractor and keep the customer relationship

quote.text: I basically built a nationwide website, and I have subcontractors who do junk removal that I get a job, I send it out to them
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

tactics.name: Anchor rental revenue with repeat B2B renters
steps: Target wedding planners, construction firms, schools and golf courses
Offer monthly rentals that need only regular cleaning

warnings.warning: Ideas are opinions; starting one does not guarantee money.

quote.text: Just because you start one of these doesn't mean you're going to make money
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

warnings.warning: Artisan trades (Venetian plaster, stucco) need real skill and apprenticeship before launching.

quote.text: You can't just start doing this. If you decide you want to start a Venetian plaster business, you need to actually learn the trade
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

warnings.warning: Licensing is required for roofing and waterproofing in many US areas.

quote.text: You need a state roofing license for this
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

warnings.warning: Keyword volumes are US figures; UK demand for several of these (generators, attic fans, crawl spaces) is much lower.

lessons.lesson: Low keyword difficulty plus weak map packs signal local service niches where a dedicated site can rank fast.

quote.text: someone making a website with riding lawn mower repair services could certainly have a chance to show up above what is showing up there already
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Specialise and name the exact service; generalist contractors often do it but don't advertise it.

quote.text: Most general contractors don't specialize in handicapped accessible remodels. Maybe they do it, but they're not advertising it
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Demographic and climate trends (ageing, outages) create growing service demand you can ride early.
Scarce skilled trades are booked out; skill scarcity is a moat.

quote.text: The people who do know how to do it, who do it well, are booked out constantly
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

lessons.lesson: Being the brand and lead source while subcontracting delivery is a common scalable home-service model.

quote.text: Pretty much every other home service you can think of, there's a company going after it with subcontractors
quote.speaker: Tim Richard

evidence_quality.rationale: Second-hand listicle based on keyword data and cited operators; promotional for his idea book.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sells an 'idea book' database linked in description.
